intrinsic_value.relativeExplain: Fair value = what the share would cost if it were priced like similar JSE companies. On profits: typical yearly profit per share (middle of the last 8 quarters x 4) x the price-to-profit multiple of the middle profitable company of the same type (financial or not). On dividends: last 12 months of dividends ÷ the dividend yield of the middle dividend payer. Fair value is the average of the two (profits alone if no dividend; none for loss-makers). Cheapest third / dearest third against it, held 3 months.
intrinsic_value.explain: Earnings-power value = normalised yearly profit ÷ (T-bill yield + 6% equity premium); dividend-discount value = last-12-month dividends grown 3% ÷ (required return − 3%). Margin of safety = value ÷ price − 1. Top third by margin of safety, held 3 months.

post_earnings_drift.explain: Strong results = latest quarter’s profit up more than 25% on the same quarter last year (and positive). Results are assumed public after the company’s usual reporting delay (60 days after quarter end if unknown; at least 90 for year end) because the JSE pages don’t carry release dates. Pullback entry = first close at least 3% below its 5-day high within 15 trading days.

support_resistance.explain: Channel = 120-day range 15–80% wide with no strong trend and at least 3 closes near both the floor and the ceiling. Buy when price is within 5% of the floor and closes up (with volume ≥1.5× its 20-day average for the volume version); sell near the ceiling, stop 5% under the floor, or after 3 months.

volume_breakout.explain: Breakout = close above the highest close of the previous 60 days on volume at least 2× (or 3×) the 20-day average. “Tight” also requires the last 20 days’ range to be under half the 120-day range and volume to have dried up beforehand.

monthEnd.verdict: edge for timing: prices tend to rise into month end and give some back early next month

calendar.explain: Pre-results = 10 trading days before results are expected to be public (quarter end + 45/90 days). Ex-dividend windows use total return (dividend added back), so a “drop” means a fall beyond the dividend. Month-end = market return on the last 3 trading days of each month vs all other days.

liquidity.explain: Accumulation = J$ value traded on up days minus down days over 20 days ÷ market value (free float isn’t published, so shares outstanding is used). Turnover surge = 20-day J$ turnover ÷ market value vs its own 6-month norm. Masked momentum ignores days with no trades.

position_sizing.explain: Top 10 by Edge score each quarter among stocks that trade at least half of days; trading costs 1.5% per side, charged only on the part of the portfolio that changes; averaged over three start dates. “Keep while top 20” only sells a holding once it drops out of the top 20.

sector_strength.explain: Relative strength = stock’s 3-month return minus its sector index (Financial, Manufacturing & Distribution, Junior Market, else the main JSE Index). Sector is assigned by which index the stock moves with most. Top third held 3 months.

bid_ask_spread.explain: Spread = (closing ask − closing bid) ÷ mid-price. Z-score compares today’s spread with its own 20-day average; a big negative z means buyers and sellers suddenly agree on price.

rates.explain: Rate regime = change in the 3-month T-bill yield over the previous 3 months (rising > +0.25 pts, falling < −0.25). Financials and Junior Market = average of those stocks vs the whole market over the next 3 months. Switch rule = hold T-bills for the next month when yields are rising, otherwise the market. Few independent periods, so treat as indicative.

fx.explain: USD/JMD 20-day change (daily rates from March 2024). “J$ weakening fast” = more than 0.5% in 20 trading days. USD-linked = stocks quoted in or paying dividends in US dollars.

insiders.explain: Parsed from the JSE’s “Trading in shares” notices (directors, senior officers, connected parties; company buybacks separately). Buy at the close of the trading day after the notice (most notices come after the 1 pm close), hold 1 or 3 months, 1.5% costs each way, compared with the average JSE stock over the same days. Big = at least J$1M and 3× the stock’s normal daily trading. Cluster = a second buy notice within a month.

events.explain: Parsed from the JSE’s dividend, split, take-over and rights-issue notices since 2018. Dividend capture: buy at the close after the declaration, sell at the close on the ex-date, dividend included; yield bands high ≥3%, mid 1.5–3%, low <1.5% of the price. Raises/cuts compare the new dividend with the same payment a year earlier (±10%, adjusted for share splits). All results after 1.5% costs each way, compared with the average JSE stock over the same days.

setups.explain: “Strong fundamentals” = top third of stocks on the Edge score’s non-price signals (cheap vs profits, dividend yield, profit growth, steady profits, no losses, below dividend value). Quiet = 3-month price change at or below the typical stock and more than 10% under its 52-week high; moving = 3-month change above the typical stock. Held 3 months vs the average JSE stock. Results-based rows pay 1.5% costs each way; “ran up” = price rose more than 5% in the month before the results.

chart.explain: Each indicator ranks all stocks; the top third is held 1 or 3 months (as labelled) against the average JSE stock, before costs. Monthly ideas would pay about 3 points in costs per round trip on top.

strategies.explain: Cheap = profit ÷ market value, profitable firms only; small = smaller half of the market by value. Dividend payers = top third by yield with no loss-making quarter in the last year; a lull = the market moved less than 5% over the previous 6 months. Book value, debt and cash-flow figures aren’t published in a machine-readable form on the JSE site, so price-to-book, ROE, leverage and accrual tests need the balance sheets read out of the PDF reports first.

balance_sheet.explain: Figures are read from each company’s PDF reports by an AI model, kept only when the balance sheet adds up and the profit agrees with the JSE’s own figure, and used only from the day the report was published. Each row holds the top third of stocks on that measure for 3 months against the average JSE stock. Debt and cash measures leave out banks, insurers and investment firms, where they mean something different.

track.explain: Each night’s Edge top 5 and top 10 are logged as shown in the app. Each day’s picks are “bought” at the next trading day’s close and held up to 3 months, dividends included, against the average JSE stock over the same days. “So far” averages every logged day with at least a week of results (days overlap, so it moves slowly); completed 3-month results subtract 1.5% costs each way.
